A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReLOAD study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReLOAD evaluations on D4RL locomotion, AntMaze, and Adroit, together with runtime measurements and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds experiments on predictor training quality and removing reward squashing.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains expert-only predictor training, rewards from negative squared embedding errors, optional exponential squashing, and subsequent offline policy learning. Newly documented initialization and normalization details do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same D4RL locomotion, AntMaze, and Adroit coverage. The new ablations use existing HalfCheetah and Walker2d datasets; they introduce no new task or input environment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in Tables 1–3, the ReLOAD+OTR comparison, and the BC comparison. The additions test internal ReLOAD configurations rather than introducing another competing method.

E3.justification: v2 adds undertrained, standard, and overtrained predictor conditions and a no-squashing control. Appendix B also revises the stated hopper-expert squashing parameter beta from 5 to 0.5. This establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendices E–F and Tables 8–9 test predictor training quality and the necessity of reward squashing across six locomotion datasets. These substantially expand validation of the method's components beyond the retained analyses of demonstration quantity, data quantity, squashing parameters, and OT integration.

E5.justification: Mean and standard deviation reporting, seed-count statements, and Appendix B's ten evaluation episodes per seed are retained. The added ablation tables use the existing uncertainty format without introducing a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: New results establish consequential sensitivities: Table 8 reports halfcheetah-medium-expert scores of 40.8 ± 1.4 with undertraining versus 92.6 ± 2.5 with standard training; Table 9 reports walker2d-medium-replay at 0.70 ± 1.0 without squashing versus 78.6 ± 2.5 with it. These are newly reported ablation findings, not performance changes between versions. Retained benchmark and appendix results are unchanged apart from equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its assumptions, proof, and mathematical conclusions remain unchanged, as do the method equations. Section 4 gains conceptual positioning against prior RND work, without adding or correcting mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion add an explicit novelty distinction between expert-transition reward inference and prior RND anti-exploration using state-action pairs. The abstract, principal contribution list, and benchmark performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion attributes undertraining failures to uninformative prediction errors, interprets overtraining results as robustness to mild overfitting, and describes squashing as a crucial regularizer against unstable reward scales. These extend v1's general stability explanation with specific failure mechanisms and qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies independent Xavier initialization of the target network and LayerNorm in both networks. Appendix B revises the hopper-expert beta value. Hardware and implementation access information are retained, while the new undertraining and overtraining budgets remain qualitative.

R1.justification: v2 adds the MOORL citation by Chaudhary et al. (2025) and expands discussion of the already cited Nikulin et al. (2023), distinguishing expert reward inference from anti-exploration. The broader related-work coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized additions explain RND positioning, transition indexing, and the shared IQL backbone, alongside two new appendix subsections. The overall narrative structure is retained. Appendix A also repeats its implementation description.

P2.justification: v2 adds two ablation tables, relocates Figure 1, redistributes existing tables, and adds publication headers. Figures and existing table designs remain largely unchanged; v1 Tables 8–11 correspond to v2 Tables 10–13.

improvement.justification: Tables 8–9 strengthen empirical support by directly testing predictor training quality and reward squashing, while the initialization and normalization disclosures improve reproducibility. The gains are limited by unspecified ablation training budgets and duplicated Appendix A prose. Overall, these additions provide useful validation without substantially changing the paper's central evidence or theory.
